newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian ex-showgirl offers swap with hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian ex-showgirl offers swap with hostages.

text.p: Former Peruvian showgirl Susy Diaz on Wednesday urged Marxist guerrillas holding 74 hostages to "make love not war" and offered to swap places with one of their hostages.

"Not only have I offered myself so that they release Foreign Minister (Francisco) Tudela, but also so that they release all the hostages inside," Diaz, now a prominent legislator and singer, told reporters.
Tudela is among the most politically valuable among the hostages still held by about 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels inside the Japanese ambassador's residence.

MRTA rebels stormed the residence on Dec. 17 and took about 500 hostages including ambassadors and senior Peruvian government officials. Most of them were later released, leaving 74 hostages remaining.

The flamboyant Diaz won election to Peru's Congress in 1995 after a raunchy election campaign during which she frequently bared her buttocks to voters -- showing a large red "13" painted on them to represent her position on the slate.

On being elected, Diaz scandalised fellow legislators with her scanty clothing in parliament, and once arrived for work on a donkey. There was no immediate response from the MRTA or government to her proposal for a swap.
